A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gluon effects, which have a strong influence on the mixing scheme, are not large enough to explain the U(1)-problem.

the current quark scheme, in which gluon effects are taken into account, provides an excellent basis for understanding the nonet mass spectrum and the mixing scheme, and for predicting electromagnetic decay rates.
the current quark model, in conjunction with the U(1)-problem, can be made to give a reasonable account of meson mass splittings, mixing angles and radiative decays.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the U(1)-problem can be solved without the need to introduce a new quark, and that the current quark model can be made consistent with experiment.
